title: The maximal-minor ideal of an injective matrix contains a nonzerodivisor
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $n,p\ge0$, and let $A$ be a $p\times n$ matrix over $R$ [def-weil-matrix]. Suppose that $v\mapsto Av$ on $R^{\oplus n}$ is injective [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Let $I$ be the ideal generated by the determinants [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] of the submatrices [def-weil-submatrix] on all columns and $n$ rows listed in increasing order. Then there exists $x\in I$ such that multiplication by $x$ on $R$ is injective. This includes $n=0$, where the empty minor is one.

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00N1 (proposition-what-exact, line 24834; Buchsbaum-Eisenbud, What makes a complex exact?, Corollary 1), implication (1) => (2) for the index i = e, where (2)(a) gives rank(phi_e) = r_e = n_e so that I(phi_e) is the ideal of n_e x n_e minors (Definition Tag 00MV, definition-rank). proof.text: Let I denote the maximal-minor ideal. If I contains no nonzerodivisor, the description of zero divisors as the union of the associated primes puts I inside that union. Finiteness and prime avoidance give an associated prime P containing I.

Localize at P. The ring S = R_P is Noetherian local and its maximal ideal is associated. Localization of the injective matrix is injective. In Lean, the coordinatewise localization maps are localized modules because localization commutes with finite products. If the mapped matrix kills the image of w, a denominator t kills Aw. Since A(tw) = t(Aw), injectivity gives tw = 0, hence w maps to zero; the localization injectivity criterion finishes. The annihilator characterization of associated primes gives z in S with a*z = 0 iff a belongs to its maximal ideal.

Apply the depth-zero unit-maximal-minor lemma to the localized matrix. Lift its increasing row selection back to A. The original determinant belongs to I and hence P; its image therefore belongs to the maximal ideal of S. RingHom.map_det identifies this image with the unit minor, a contradiction. For zero columns the same argument uses the empty determinant; the zero ring causes no exception, since its identity is a nonzerodivisor.

lean.statement: theorem exists_nonZeroDivisor_mem_maximal_minors {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] {n p : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin n) R) (hinj : Function.Injective A.mulVec) : ∃ x : R, x ∈ Ideal.span {d : R | ∃ r : Fin n → Fin p, StrictMono r ∧ d = (A.submatrix r id).det} ∧ x ∈ nonZeroDivisors R
